learn: Meter is how beats are grouped.
The time signature at the start of music tells the meter. The top number tells how many beats in each measure.
4/4 has four beats per measure. 3/4 has three. 2/4 has two.
check: What does the top number of a time signature tell?
How many beats per measure in 3/4?
lessons.try: Conduct 4/4 by moving your hand down, left, right, up.

learn: The first beat of each measure is usually the strongest, called the downbeat.
In 4/4, beat 3 is medium strong. Beats 2 and 4 are weak.
Many rock and pop songs clap on 2 and 4, called the backbeat.
check: The first beat of a measure is the...
The backbeat is usually on beats...
lessons.try: Clap on 2 and 4 while a song plays.

learn: Conductors show meter with hand patterns.
The 2 pattern goes down-up. The 3 pattern goes down-right-up, like a triangle.
The downbeat always moves down.
lessons.try: Conduct a 3/4 waltz while it plays.

learn: In 4/4 time, a whole note gets 4 beats, a half note 2, a quarter note 1, and an eighth note half a beat.
Two eighths equal one quarter. Two quarters equal one half. Two halves equal one whole.
This is like fractions in math.
check: How many quarter notes equal a half note?
How many beats does an eighth note get in 4/4?
lessons.try: Write a measure using one half note and two quarter notes.

learn: A dot after a note adds half of its value.
A dotted half note gets 2 + 1 = 3 beats.
Dotted half notes often fill a whole measure of 3/4.
check: A dotted half fills a measure of...
lessons.try: Clap a dotted half note while counting "1, 2, 3".

learn: Four sixteenth notes equal one quarter note. Say "ti-ka-ti-ka".
Every note has a matching rest of the same length.
A whole rest hangs from a line. A half rest sits on a line.
check: Does every note have a matching rest?
lessons.try: Clap "ta, ti-ka-ti-ka, ti-ti, ta".

learn: The treble clef, or G clef, curls around the second line, which is G.
Line notes from bottom to top are E, G, B, D, F: "Every Good Boy Does Fine".
Space notes spell FACE.
check: The treble clef is also called the...
The lines of the treble staff are...
lessons.try: Write the letter names of five notes on a treble staff.

learn: Music uses seven letters: A, B, C, D, E, F, G. Then it repeats.
Going up the staff moves forward in the alphabet. Going down moves backward.
Middle C sits on a short line below the treble staff, called a ledger line.
check: How many letters in the musical alphabet?
lessons.try: Find middle C on a piano or keyboard app.

learn: A sharp (♯) raises a note by a half step. A flat (♭) lowers it by a half step.
On a piano, the black keys are sharps and flats.
A natural sign (♮) cancels a sharp or flat.
check: Raises a note a half step
Lowers a note a half step
What cancels a sharp or flat?
lessons.try: Find F sharp and B flat on a keyboard.

learn: A scale is a set of notes in order going up or down.
The C major scale uses only white keys: C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C.
In solfege: do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do.
lessons.try: Play or sing the C major scale up and down.

learn: The distance between two notes is called an interval.
A step is a second (C to D). A skip is a third (C to E).
Larger leaps include the fifth (C to G) and the octave (C to the next C).
check: The distance between two notes is an...
C to the next C is an...
lessons.try: Sing do to sol (a fifth) and do to high do (an octave).

learn: Major scales and melodies often sound bright or happy.
Minor scales often sound dark or sad.
Composers choose major or minor to create mood.
check: Composers choose major or minor to create...
lessons.try: Listen to "Twinkle, Twinkle" in major, then a minor version. Describe the change.

learn: From softest to loudest: pp, p, mp, mf, f, ff.
Accents (>) above a note mean play that note with extra force.
Sforzando (sfz) means a sudden strong accent.
check: Which is louder: mp or mf?
lessons.try: Clap a rhythm and accent every fourth note.

learn: Largo is very slow. Adagio is slow. Andante is walking speed.
Moderato is moderate. Allegro is fast. Presto is very fast.
Tempo is measured in beats per minute (BPM) with a metronome.
lessons.try: Use a metronome app to clap at 60, 90 and 120 BPM.

learn: Musicians combine dynamics, tempo and articulation to express feeling.
Legato means smooth and connected. Staccato means short and detached.
The same melody can feel very different with different expression.
lessons.try: Sing "Mary Had a Little Lamb" legato, then staccato.

learn: A round is a song where groups start at different times, singing the same melody.
"Frère Jacques" and "Row, Row, Row Your Boat" are famous rounds.
When the parts overlap, they create harmony.
check: The same melody at different times
lessons.try: Sing "Frère Jacques" as a round with two groups.

learn: Partner songs are two different songs that sound good sung together.
An ostinato is a short pattern repeated over and over under a melody.
Ostinatos can be rhythmic or melodic.
lessons.try: Sing a melody while a partner repeats a short ostinato.

learn: Harmony is two or more notes sounding at the same time.
A chord is three or more notes played together. C, E and G make a C major chord.
Harmony adds richness to melodies.
check: C, E and G make a...
lessons.try: Play C, E and G together on a keyboard.

learn: A symphony orchestra has four sections: strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion.
Strings are the largest section, sitting in front.
The concertmaster, the lead violinist, tunes the orchestra.
check: How many sections in an orchestra?
lessons.try: Draw a seating chart of an orchestra.

learn: Each family has high and low instruments.
Strings: violin (high), viola, cello, double bass (low). Brass: trumpet (high), French horn, trombone, tuba (low).
Woodwinds: piccolo (highest), flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon (low).
check: Which string is between violin and cello?
lessons.try: Listen to a piccolo and a tuba. Describe their ranges.

learn: Benjamin Britten's "The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra" (1946) introduces each section.
Listen for which instruments play the melody.
Symphonies are long works for orchestra, often in four movements.
check: Who wrote "The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra"?
When listening, notice which instruments play the...
lessons.try: Listen to part of Britten's "Young Person's Guide" and name the instruments you hear.

learn: Binary form is AB: two contrasting sections.
Ternary form is ABA: the first section returns.
Many minuets and folk dances use these forms.
lessons.try: Listen to a minuet and identify A and B sections.

learn: Rondo form returns to A between contrasting sections: ABACA.
Theme and variations states a melody, then changes it in different ways.
Mozart wrote variations on the tune we know as "Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star" (around 1781).
lessons.try: Listen to Mozart's variations on "Twinkle, Twinkle" and count the changes.

learn: An introduction comes before the main music starts.
An interlude is a short section between parts.
A coda is an ending section that wraps up the piece.
check: What comes at the very end?
lessons.try: Add an introduction and a coda to a song you know.

learn: The Baroque era lasted about 1600 to 1750.
Johann Sebastian Bach wrote complex music with many melodies woven together.
Antonio Vivaldi wrote "The Four Seasons", violin concertos for each season.
lessons.try: Listen to "Spring" from Vivaldi's "The Four Seasons". What do you hear?

learn: The Classical era lasted about 1750 to 1820.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart began composing as a young child and wrote over 600 works.
Classical music is known for clear melodies and balanced forms.
check: Who began composing as a young child?
lessons.try: Listen to Mozart's "Eine kleine Nachtmusik" and hum the main theme.

learn: The Romantic era (about 1820 to 1900) focused on emotion and storytelling.
Ludwig van Beethoven bridged Classical and Romantic. He kept composing even after becoming deaf.
Pyotr Tchaikovsky wrote "The Nutcracker" ballet (1892).
check: Who kept composing after becoming deaf?
lessons.try: Listen to "Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy" and name the twinkly instrument (the celesta).

learn: Spirituals were songs created by enslaved African Americans, expressing faith and hope for freedom.
Jazz began in New Orleans in the early 1900s, mixing African and European traditions.
Bluegrass and country music grew from Appalachian folk traditions.
lessons.try: Listen to a jazz recording and notice the improvised solos.

learn: Indian classical music uses ragas (melodic patterns) and talas (rhythm cycles).
Andean music from South America features panpipes and charangos.
Steel drums (steelpan) were invented in Trinidad and Tobago in the 1930s.
lessons.try: Listen to steelpan music and describe its sound.

learn: Music is used in celebrations, worship, work, protest and entertainment.
Work songs helped people keep a steady pace together.
Songs like "We Shall Overcome" united people in the Civil Rights Movement.
check: "We Shall Overcome" was sung during the...
lessons.try: Make a list of times music plays a role in your family's life.
